articles.title: South Africa v Australia: second men’s cricket Test, day three – live
articles.summary: Updates as the Proteas host Australia at St George’s Park. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. 47th over: South Africa 106-5 (Bavuma 42, Mulder 10) Bavuma looks intent on settling in. Cummins gives him a couple of bouncers, but he’s very happy to get out of the way.
body: 57th over: South Africa 151-6 (Bavuma 52, Jansen 31) Beats him! Boland shows Jansen what he has in his locker, classic Boland seam away, so nearly the edge. Then goes at Jansen with the short ball again, a nasty one up at the gloves, but Jansen manages to play it down off glove and bat handle into the leg side and escape the strike. Drinks.

56th over: South Africa 150-6 (Bavuma 52, Jansen 30) Three singles from Starc’s over. Given the Hazlewood absence we’ll be seeing Webster Time soon. Still 24 overs from a possible new ball – break this stand and it may not be needed.

55th over: South Africa 147-6 (Bavuma 51, Jansen 28) You can hit Scotty Boland! Jansen channels a bit of the England approach from 2023. It’s not an overpitched ball exactly, but Jansen is so tall that his straight drive is able to meet it a shorter time after it lands. Very clean straight drive clears long off for six. Boland puts square leg back and goes the bouncer, and Jansen resists, just.

articles.title: Irwin backs himself to bounce back after 'hard' year
articles.summary: Glenn Irwin believes he can return to the front of the British Superbike Championship, with an exciting move to Michael Laverty's BMW-backed team providing fresh motivation for 2027.
body: The 12-time North West 200 Superbike race winner will ride an Alpha Racing-prepared BMW M 1000 RR for the GRYD Racing team, co-owned by Laverty and David Eltherington.

The 36-year-old Northern Ireland rider admits 2026 failed to live up to expectations as injuries, crashes, technical issues and a difficult relationship with Ducati's new Panigale V4R, combined to derail his title ambitions.

Despite showing flashes of his speed with a podium at Knockhill and success at the North West 200, Irwin was left searching for answers throughout a frustrating campaign and ended 14th in the series standings.
The Carrickfergus rider has twice finished runner-up in BSB, including being pipped by half-a-point by then teammate Tommy Bridewell in 2023.

articles.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
articles.summary: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker. Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player.
body: The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media.

He is tired of the shorthand way he is described during these high‑profile job hunts. People focus on his playing accolades, including calling him the treble winner, a label he says belongs to one season in a run of three Premier League titles at Manchester United from 1999-2001. “I’m a manager,” he says.

Over the past four years, Yorke has quietly built a coaching résumé far removed from Old Trafford. His first taste of management came in May 2022, taking charge of Australia’s A-League All Stars against Barcelona in front of more than 70,000 people in Sydney. They lost 3-2. “I realised then that I enjoyed it,” he says.

Macarthur, based in Sydney, followed that July. “We went to a relatively unknown team in the A‑League and managed to win the cup.” The Australia Cup success, three months into his spell, was the club’s first trophy.

articles.summary: Isaac appears to back current direction of world governing body. But ‘premature’ to talk about support for Gianni Infantino. Football Australia chair Anter Isaac has played down concerns around the controversial World Cup privatisation push engineered by Gianni Infantino ahead of a meeting of Asian…
body: Isaac’s sentiments come amid a global rebound in support for the embattled Fifa president, who at one stage appeared unlikely to be able to continue in his role following criticism led by officials in Europe and North America.
The Swiss lawyer now enjoys backing from South America, Africa and growing chunks of Asia, which would represent a bloc large enough for him to win March’s Fifa presidential election.

Continental powerbrokers are converging on Tokyo this week for the Asian Football Confederation congress. Fifa’s leadership and governance do not form part of the formal meeting agenda, but will be discussed by those present alongside the likelihood of January’s Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia going ahead.

Isaac, the most senior football official in Australia, was asked about the situation at Fifa in an episode of a little-known sports business You Tube channel earlier this month that has been viewed fewer than 200 times.

articles.title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence
articles.summary: British long-distance runner Jake Smith was enduring a relentless pattern of race, illness, injury, repeat - he had no idea he had REDs and was under-fuelling.
body: That is what doctors told British long-distance runner Jake Smith four years ago.
By the age of 23, he had signed a professional contract with Nike and represented Great Britain on the global stage.
But at the same time, his body was deteriorating - enduring a relentless pattern of race, illness, injury, repeat.

Balancing an intense training regime with disordered eating meant the 28-year-old returned from a running camp in Uganda weighing just eight stone (51kg) at 5ft 5in (1.7m). He had such brittle bones that he was told his career could be over.

articles.title: 49ers' offense goes cold after Mike Evans exits. What does that mean going forward?
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers' loss of wide receiver Mike Evans to an Achilles injury Monday during a 23-17 win slowed the offense. Is it an omen or just another thing that QB Brock Purdy will overcome?
body: On Monday night, late in the third quarter, with his team leading by 20 points and another 300-yard performance seemingly assured, Brock Purdy looked, well, relaxed.

With his defense on the field, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback sat alone at the end of a bench, glancing occasionally at the Jumbotron, without a Microsoft tablet in his hands and with his quarterbacks coach, Mick Lombardi, standing about 10 feet away. At one point, Purdy crossed his legs. Later, he dangled his feet in the air and moved them from side to side, keeping them loose.

About an hour later, outside the 49ers' locker room, Purdy was asked about the solitary moment when he wasn't studying the opponent's defense or conferring with his position coach. Was that unusual for him during a game? Purdy only had a vague memory.
"With the tablet, there's only so much you can look at," Purdy said. "It was a long drive. I was probably just getting off my feet and taking a breath."

articles.title: ‘Jeremiah’s to lose’ – Heisman Trophy rankings on social media spark interesting discussion
articles.summary: Despite Jeremiah Smith being the frontrunner for the Heisman Trophy this year, a ranking of the top 10 players competing for the award has led to some interesting online discourse.
body: Jeremiah Smith has emerged as the frontrunner in the 2026 Heisman Trophy race, putting up 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns in seven games for Ohio State. The Buckeyes star is chasing history as he looks to become the first wide receiver to win the award since DeVonta Smith in 2020.

It is never that simple, though. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah and Ole Miss man Trinidad Chambliss are putting together strong cases of their own. Other names like Notre Dame’s CJ Carr and Georgia’s Gunner Stockton have also been thrown around before, but they haven’t made this list.

Seven weeks into the season, lots of teams are enjoying strong starts, thanks to some of the stars who are looking to win the Heisman. The Rebels’ success has been attributed to Chambliss, while the Tennessee Volunteers’ wins have seen DeSean Bishop enter the conversation.
On Monday, On3 shared their rankings for the top 10 college players in contention for the award, and fans responded to the list with some expected takes, but also some truly unique ones.

articles.title: Boulter puts rain delays behind her to progress at Japan Open
articles.summary: A day after heavy rainfall caused play to be suspended, Britain's Katie Boulter returned to clinch a 6-3 6-1 victory at the Japan Open over wildcard Himeno Sakatsume.
body: The world No 58 concluded a dominant victory in one hour and 32 minutes in Osaka, and she will next face Swiss player Viktorija Golubic for a place in the quarter-finals.

The victory gives Boulter a 20-20 record across her last 40 matches, and a confidence boost following a period in which she has only played three matches since September 30, owing to early exits at the China Open (second round) and Wuhan Open (first round).

On Monday, the match between Boulter and Sakatsume had barely started when the players were forced off court after torrential rain arrived in Osaka. Given the venue didn't have a roof, the court was open to all of the elements.
By that point, only three games had been played in the first set, with Sakatsume leading 2-1 at the time of the suspension.

articles.title: Six of the best free transfers in Premier League history
articles.summary: In an era when Premier League clubs routinely shatter transfer records, a successful free transfer can still represent outstanding business. Jean-Marc Bosman helped change football forever with the landmark ruling that bears his name in 1995.
body: Some signings can transform a club's image entirely, and Ruud Gullit fits that brief. The Ballon d'Or winner pitched up in West London in the mid-nineties, at a time when Chelsea found themselves perennially marooned in mid-table.

Gullit made an immediate impression and finished runner-up for the 1995/96 FWA Footballer of the Year award, with the Dutch icon's impact paving the path for an eclectic collection of overseas stars, such as Gianluca Vialli and Gianfranco Zola, to head to Stamford Bridge.
Arguably the best free-transfer signing in Premier League history, and certainly one of its most controversial.
There was genuine astonishment when Arsene Wenger paraded Sol Campbell as Arsenal 's latest signing, with the Gunners having swooped to sign the England defender from bitter rivals Tottenham.

articles.title: England unchanged for World Cup clash vs France with Lewis absent again
articles.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man squad that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga in the tournament opener for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup clash against France.
body: AJ Brimson retains the job at full-back with Jack Welsby again named as an interchange, while Luke Thompson starts at prop in the absence of Morgan Knowles, who suffered an injury in the lead-up to the opening game against Tonga.
Veteran centre Kallum Watkins is listed among the reserves as he chases a cap at his fourth World Cup, while there also remains no place in the squad for Mikey Lewis.
As per World Cup rules, each side is able to name a six-player bench in each game, but only four of the six players named can be brought on.
Last weekend against Tonga, Welsby and Warrington Wolves winger Matty Ashton were the unused substitutes - with Wigan Warriors speedster Zach Eckersley getting the nod instead.

articles.title: Reese scores 30 points as Atlanta win at Golden State to level WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals after she struggled down the stretch in the series opener, as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries at both ends in the second half to win 79-65 and level the best-of-seven series at 1-1.
body: In front of the Valkyries' raucous home crowd, the Atlanta star had no choice but to raise her voice - and Reese knew she had to raise her game, too.
"For me, I think I let my team down last game not really contributing as much as I could in the second half," Reese said.

"Not even just about scoring, my screen quality, me hustling and running to get rebounds, just doing the things that they know me to do. So I just wanted to make sure I came out tonight and left my mark and did whatever I could to get the win, and I think I did that tonight."

Rhyne Howard set a Finals record with six steals, Allisha Gray added 18 points, and Jordin Canada contributed 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds as the Dream earned the franchise's first Finals victory after going winless in three previous trips - 0-10 overall.
